domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk's primary focus is Command Code, a coding agent that learns developer taste and writes code matching personal preferences, fitting coding_agents_software_engineering. Command Code is a coding assistant product built on the Langbase developer platform for software builders. The talk covers deployment at scale (1.2B agent runs/month) and evaluation through side-by-side CLI demo comparisons. Requires familiarity with CLI tooling, TypeScript, coding agents, and neuro-symbolic RL concepts. A conference presentation with live demos, delivered at AI Engineer. All claims are drawn directly from transcript excerpts with said_in_transcript grade.

summary: Ahmad Awais presents Command Code, a coding agent designed to develop taste by learning from how a developer writes and edits code. He begins with a demo comparing Claude Code and Command Code building a CLI for ISO date output. Command Code automatically applies Awais's preferences—TypeScript, tsup, pnpm, vitest, commander, lowercase hyphen-v version flags, separate commands directory, and 0.0.1 starting version—none explicitly specified. Claude Code produces generic output with console.log and 1.0.0. Command Code stores learned preferences in a taste file inside a command code folder, described as intuition built into a meta neuro-symbolic architecture that is more deterministic than pure LLM output. Awais traces his journey from 2020 GPT-3 access through building Langbase (which raised $5 million led by GitHub's founder), now processing 700 terabytes and 1.2 billion agent runs monthly. He identifies AI's core problem: it is lazy and sloppy by default, optimizing for correctness rather than style. He critiques rules files like CLAUDE.md as insufficient, comparing them to a justice system where rules alone need human judgment. The meta neuro-symbolic approach combines deterministic architecture with reinforcement learning, using a KL divergence loop for continuous correction from explicit and implicit feedback. Reflective context engineering makes the system self-aware, automatically updating preferences when a developer changes habits—for example, switching from meow to commander for CLI building. Awais envisions sharing taste profiles: borrowing a design engineer's taste for frontend work, or using Tanner's React taste from TanStack. Command Code launched today at commandcode.ai, with taste installable via npx. Internally at Langbase, the tool has 10xed code merge throughput and significantly reduced pull request review time. His central thesis: good code is about an invisible architecture of choices, not just correctness, and taste models represent the next frontier of coding.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Demo Motivation
sections.summary: Ahmad Awais introduces himself and Command Code, a coding agent with taste. He recounts his background: 20 years building, Shades of Purple code theme, NASA Mars Ingenuity contribution, and 5 years in LLM space. He wants coding agents to learn from him, understand his preferences, and adapt to his invisible architecture of choices.

sections.title: CLI Demo: Command Code vs Claude Code
sections.summary: Awais demos building a CLI for ISO date output with both Claude Code and Command Code. Command Code automatically uses tsup, TypeScript, pnpm, ASCII banner, commander, lowercase hyphen-v version, separate commands directory, vitest, and 0.0.1 starting version. Claude Code produces generic output with console.log and 1.0.0, missing all preferences.

sections.title: Taste File and Architecture Explanation
sections.summary: Awais reveals the taste file inside a command code folder containing learned CLI preferences—none written by him. He describes it as intuition built into a meta neuro-symbolic model, a deterministic architecture that remixes his preferences rather than spec or scale.

sections.title: Origin Story and Langbase Scale
sections.summary: Awais traces the journey from 2020 GPT-3 access to building Langbase, raising $5 million led by GitHub's founder. Langbase processes 700 terabytes and 1.2 billion agent runs monthly. He identifies AI's core problem: it is lazy and sloppy by default, requiring repeated prompting to get desired output.

sections.title: Vibe Coding and Rules Files Critique
sections.summary: Awais critiques the state of agents: 150,000 vibe-coded in five months, but vibe coding isn't better than a developer's own rules. He argues rules files like CLAUDE.md and agents.md are insufficient, comparing them to a justice system where rules alone need human lawyers, judges, and juries. He calls for agents that acquire taste rather than follow rules.

sections.title: Taste as Acquired Preference
sections.summary: Awais presents Command Code as a coding agent with acquired taste, showing examples like preferring JavaScript object parameters when more than two parameters exist. He contrasts Claude Code's generic sum.js output with Command Code's preference-aware output, concluding that good code is about an invisible architecture of choices, not just correctness.

sections.title: Meta Neuro-Symbolic Architecture and Continuous Learning
sections.summary: Awais details the meta neuro-symbolic reasoning space with reinforcement learning. Neuro-symbolic architecture is more deterministic and explainable than probabilistic transformers. The system uses a KL divergence loop for correction and learns from both explicit and implicit feedback. Reflective context engineering makes it self-aware—automatically detecting habit changes like switching from meow to commander for CLI building, updating taste without manual intervention. He envisions sharing taste profiles across developers and teams.

sections.title: Taste Sharing, Launch, and Results
sections.summary: Awais envisions borrowing taste from notable developers like Tanner's React taste or a design engineer's frontend taste. Command Code launches today at commandcode.ai with taste installable via npx. Internally at Langbase, the tool 10xed code merge throughput and significantly reduced PR review time. He positions taste models as capturing the world's intuition and intentions, representing the next frontier of coding beyond LLM-captured world knowledge.
